correctness.rationale: Reconstructed source framework: Theorem 7.4 identifies equal loci with proportional nonzero Jacobian conics; Proposition 7.1 ensures nonzero Jacobian; Theorem 7.5 proof gives G_i for shared pair and nets span{1,F,G_i}. After rescaling G_2, J(F,G_2-G_1)=0. For F=(Y-alpha)(Y-beta), direct derivatives in k[X,Y] give J(F,H)=-(2Y-alpha-beta)(2aX+bY+r), a nonzero factor for characteristic !=2, hence a=b=r=0 and ker=span{1,F,Y}. It follows the difference has unique lambda mod span{1,F}. Equality of nets forces coefficient C=1 by the normalized nonzero Jacobians, proving iff entangled. Explicit Example 7.6: G_t/4-G_p=-3/2-F/4+3Y/2. Coincident parallel lines alpha=beta, finite fields of odd characteristic and dependent coefficient conditions are included. The general proof does not rely on SymPy verify.py exit status.

value.rationale: Motivated narrow structural completion rather than a textbook exercise for its own sake: Theorem 7.5 gives exact reconstruction from one nonparallel bisector pair and Example 7.6 witnesses failure for parallel pairs. The new statement classifies the *entire* ambiguity space for all parallel pairs over all odd-characteristic fields and gives a necessary-and-sufficient vanishing test for entanglement, so it locates the precise boundary of uniqueness. This one-dimensional obstruction is a natural object/invariant for future work on quadrangle net reconstruction and moduli; no geometric existence/realization theorem is asserted. The argument is extremely short and its research value modest, but an exact motivated missing-case structural lemma meets the uniform standard; neither dramatic downstream work nor paper-sized scope is required.
